summary.text: Xeronema callistemon is a species of flowering plant endemic to the Poor Knights Islands and Taranga Island in the north of New Zealand. It was discovered in 1924 and is also called raupōtaranga or Poor Knights lily. The plant is listed as vulnerable in the 1997 IUCN Red List of Plants, but As of April 2026 is not listed in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

summary.text: Howea belmoreana, the curly palm, kentia palm, or Belmore sentry palm, is a species of flowering plant in the family Arecaceae, endemic to Lord Howe Island, Australia. It and Howea forsteriana probably evolved from a common ancestor through sympatric speciation. The canopy of a mature kentia palm tree spreads 5–10 ft (2–3 m) in diameter and contains roughly 36 leaves.

gbif.occurrences.detail: GBIF occurrence download https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.hbdw64, of 2026-10-21; records tested against the native regions' shapes, openly licensed and restricted alike (Natural Earth 1:10m states and provinces (public domain), placed in TDWG's level-3 regions (WGSRPD second edition) by TDWG's tables and gazetteer; shapes rule r85); a record within the margin or off a coast counted only on no other region's land and in the region's own country; 4 records within 1 km of a botanic garden, herbarium or zoo left out (4 at a botanic garden or arboretum; Wikidata's list)
